title: Leaving the Preposition at the End
goal: Ask questions and make relative clauses with the preposition in natural Bokmål position.

objectives.statement: Ask questions and make relative clauses with the preposition in natural Bokmål position.

spans.value: Maja and Jonas are preparing a small party in their shared flat. They need music, but they do not own the right equipment.
Har du sett den blå høyttaleren som vi hørte på i butikken?

blocks.translation: Have you seen the blue speaker that we listened to in the shop?

spans.value: Ja, men den var dyr. Vet du hvem vi kan låne en høyttaler av?

blocks.translation: Yes, but it was expensive. Do you know who we can borrow a speaker from?

spans.value: Kanskje Sindre. Han er naboen som jeg lånte projektoren av i fjor.

blocks.translation: Maybe Sindre. He is the neighbour whom I borrowed the projector from last year.

spans.value: God idé. Hva skal vi koble høyttaleren til?

blocks.translation: Good idea. What are we going to connect the speaker to?

spans.value: Den lille laptopen på kjøkkenbordet.

blocks.translation: The small laptop on the kitchen table.

spans.value: Og hvem skal vi lage spillelista sammen med?

blocks.translation: And who are we going to make the playlist with?

spans.value: Lea. Hun kjenner mange sanger som folk liker å danse til.

blocks.translation: Lea. She knows lots of songs that people like dancing to.

spans.value: Several expressions in this conversation contain a preposition:

no.value: høre på noe

en.value: listen to something

no.value: låne noe av noen

en.value: borrow something from someone

no.value: koble noe til noe

en.value: connect something to something

no.value: gjøre noe sammen med noen

en.value: do something together with someone

spans.value: When Maja and Jonas ask about the missing person or thing, that information moves to the beginning of the question. The preposition normally remains in its natural place later in the sentence.
A word such as av, med, om, på or til is a preposition (preposisjon). In ordinary statements, it usually comes before the person or thing connected to it.

no.value: Vi kan låne høyttaleren av Sindre.

en.value: We can borrow the speaker from Sindre.

no.value: Vi skal koble høyttaleren til laptopen.

en.value: We are going to connect the speaker to the laptop.

spans.value: When the person or thing becomes the focus of a question, the question word moves to the beginning. The preposition stays behind. This pattern is called preposition stranding.

no.value: Hvem kan vi låne høyttaleren av?

en.value: Who can we borrow the speaker from?

no.value: Hva skal vi koble høyttaleren til?

en.value: What are we going to connect the speaker to?

spans.value: The same thing happens when the person or thing is described by a relative clause.

no.value: Sindre er naboen som vi kan låne høyttaleren av.

en.value: Sindre is the neighbour whom we can borrow the speaker from.

no.value: Dette er laptopen som vi skal koble høyttaleren til.

en.value: This is the laptop that we are going to connect the speaker to.

spans.value: The compact rule is:

statement.value: Put the question word at the beginning of a question, or the described person or thing before the relative clause. Leave the associated preposition in its normal position later in the clause.

spans.value: Begin with an ordinary statement and notice which noun phrase follows the preposition.

no.value: Du snakker med Nora.

en.value: You are talking with Nora.

spans.value: If Nora is the unknown person, replace her with hvem and move hvem to the beginning. Keep med behind.

no.value: Hvem snakker du med?

en.value: Who are you talking with?

spans.value: The ordinary question word order still applies after the question word.

no.value: Dere snakker om festen.

en.value: You are talking about the party.

no.value: Hva snakker dere om?

en.value: What are you talking about?

no.value: Hun venter på en kollega.

en.value: She is waiting for a colleague.

no.value: Hvem venter hun på?

en.value: Who is she waiting for?

no.value: De bor i det gule huset.

en.value: They live in the yellow house.

no.value: Hvilket hus bor de i?

en.value: Which house do they live in?

spans.value: The question word can be followed by a noun, as in hvilket hus. The principle remains the same: huset is connected to i, so i stays later in the question.
Compare these two questions:

no.value: Hvem snakker med Maja?

en.value: Who is talking with Maja?

no.value: Hvem snakker Maja med?

en.value: Who is Maja talking with?

spans.value: In the first question, hvem is the person doing the talking. The phrase med Maja remains complete.
In the second, Maja is doing the talking. Hvem represents the person connected to med, so med is stranded later in the question.
It is possible to place some prepositions before the question word:

no.value: Med hvem snakket du?

en.value: With whom did you speak?

spans.value: This sounds formal or marked in many everyday situations. Natural conversational Bokmål normally prefers:

no.value: Hvem snakket du med?

en.value: Who did you speak with?

spans.value: Use the stranded pattern as the ordinary spoken and neutral everyday model.

sections.title: Describing people and things with relative clauses

spans.value: A relative clause (relativsetning) identifies or describes a person or thing.
Start with two statements:

no.value: Jeg snakket med naboen. Naboen har en høyttaler.

en.value: I spoke with the neighbour. The neighbour has a speaker.

spans.value: The repeated noun can become the person described by a relative clause:

no.value: Naboen som jeg snakket med, har en høyttaler.

en.value: The neighbour whom I spoke with has a speaker.

spans.value: Naboen appears before the relative clause. Inside the clause, med remains where the complete phrase med naboen would normally occur.
The same pattern works with things and places:

no.value: Vi hørte på høyttaleren.

en.value: We listened to the speaker.

no.value: Dette er høyttaleren som vi hørte på.

en.value: This is the speaker that we listened to.

no.value: Gjestene skal være i dette rommet.

en.value: The guests are going to be in this room.

no.value: Dette er rommet som gjestene skal være i.

en.value: This is the room that the guests are going to be in.

no.value: Folk liker å danse til denne sangen.

en.value: People like dancing to this song.

no.value: Dette er sangen som folk liker å danse til.

en.value: This is the song that people like dancing to.

spans.value: Not every relative clause contains a stranded preposition:

no.value: Lea kjenner en musiker som bor i Bergen.

en.value: Lea knows a musician who lives in Bergen.

spans.value: Here som represents the person who lives in Bergen. It is not connected to a preposition.
Compare:

no.value: Lea kjenner musikeren som Jonas snakket om.

en.value: Lea knows the musician whom Jonas talked about.

spans.value: Here musikeren is connected to om in the underlying expression snakke om noen. Om therefore remains later in the relative clause.
Do not remove the preposition
The verb or expression still requires its preposition.

no.value: Hva snakker dere om?

en.value: What are you talking about?

no.value: ✗ Hva snakker dere?

en.value: ✗ What are you talking?

spans.value: Without om, snakker normally lacks the intended meaning of talking about a topic.
Similarly:

no.value: Dette er sangen som alle danser til.

en.value: This is the song that everyone dances to.

no.value: ✗ Dette er sangen som alle danser.

en.value: ✗ This is the song that everyone dances.

spans.value: Do not repeat the person or thing
Once hvem or the described noun supplies the missing information, do not add an extra pronoun after the preposition.

no.value: Hvem snakket du med?

en.value: Who did you speak with?

no.value: ✗ Hvem snakket du med ham?

en.value: ✗ Who did you speak with him?

spans.value: Likewise:

no.value: Dette er naboen som jeg lånte verktøyet av.

en.value: This is the neighbour whom I borrowed the tool from.

no.value: ✗ Dette er naboen som jeg lånte verktøyet av ham.

en.value: ✗ This is the neighbour whom I borrowed the tool from him.

spans.value: Do not move every preposition to the sentence end
Only the preposition connected to the questioned or described element is stranded.

no.value: Hvem var du på kino med i går?

en.value: Who were you at the cinema with yesterday?

spans.value: Med is not literally the last word because i går gives extra time information. It is still stranded: the person who would normally follow med has moved to the beginning.

no.value: Dette er vennen som jeg var på kino med i går.

en.value: This is the friend whom I was at the cinema with yesterday.

spans.value: Think of the preposition as staying in its natural grammatical position, not as being forced to become the final word.
Sindre arrives with a speaker and several cables.
Er dette kabelen som dere lette etter?

blocks.translation: Is this the cable that you were looking for?

spans.value: Ja, det er den! Her er laptopen som vi skal koble høyttaleren til.

blocks.translation: Yes, that is the one! Here is the laptop that we are going to connect the speaker to.

spans.value: Flott. Hvem skal dere lage spillelista sammen med?

blocks.translation: Great. Who are you going to make the playlist with?

spans.value: Lea. Men hun sendte tre spillelister, og jeg vet ikke hvilken vi skal høre på.

blocks.translation: Lea. But she sent three playlists, and I do not know which one we should listen to.

spans.value: Velg den som folk kan danse til.

blocks.translation: Choose the one that people can dance to.

spans.value: The continuation uses the same pattern for two purposes: asking for missing information and identifying a particular person or thing.
Imagine that two colleagues are organizing a work trip. They need to identify the hotel, the colleague they will travel with, the train they are waiting for and the meeting they have been invited to.

prompt.value: Read the everyday question and choose the analysis that identifies the linked question word and preposition and distinguishes it from a subject question.

options.text: Hvem snakket du med? (Who did you speak with?) — med is an isolated final word and has no connection to hvem.
options.why: Med belongs to the question phrase represented by hvem.

options.text: Hvem snakket du med? (Who did you speak with?) — hvem is linked to med; med remains later, unlike a subject question with no stranded preposition.
options.why: The taught everyday pattern moves hvem to the beginning and keeps med after the verb.

options.text: Hvem snakket du med? (Who did you speak with?) — hvem is the subject and med is linked to du.
options.why: The sentence asks about the person connected to med, not the subject.

stem.value: Which analysis correctly identifies the question word and the preposition connected to it?

prompt.value: Combine the two statements into one natural Bokmål sentence. Put the shared noun before som and keep the preposition inside the relative clause. Statements: Jeg snakket med naboen. Naboen har en høyttaler. (I spoke with the neighbour. The neighbour has a speaker.)
Select the one token that is wrong/needs changing.

payload.feedback: Remove the repeated pronoun ham. The natural Bokmål repair is Hvem snakket du med?; the initial question word already supplies the person linked to med.

prompt.value: A colleague needs to identify the train the travelers are waiting for. Build one complete natural Bokmål question with the question phrase first and the associated preposition later.

Combine these new work-trip statements into one natural Bokmål sentence with a relative clause: Vi snakket om møtet. Dette er møtet. (We talked about the meeting. This is the meeting.) Keep the preposition inside the clause.

Without looking back, write in natural Bokmål: one question and one sentence with a relative clause. Use different prepositions in the two sentences. After each sentence, briefly state which earlier question word or noun the preposition connects to.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for every criterion. Accept different natural Bokmål wording and any taught prepositions, provided the two prepositions differ and their connections and positions are clear.

criteria.instruction: Writes one natural Bokmål question with the question word or phrase early and its required preposition later.
Writes one natural Bokmål sentence with a relative clause, with the described noun before the clause and the required preposition retained inside it.
Uses different prepositions in the question and the relative-clause sentence.
Briefly states in Norwegian which earlier question word or noun each preposition connects to.
